title: Clonin' Keys, Makin' Gs Walkthrough - IGN
content:
Randy calls Lucia and Jason and asks them to steal a Granforma Zorrusso. This Grand Theft Auto VI Chapter 3 mission is a tutorial for a pivotal tool: the Key Cloner, and this official IGN GTA 6 guide walks you through it. This mission can be completed solo or as a pair. It’s a quick one – or at least it should be! Once you arrive at the apartment parking lot, you’ll call Randy for more information. He’ll have one of his guys send you an app for the Key Cloner. Download it, then you’re good to start hunting for the Granforma. You’ll find the red Granforma Zorrusso tucked away in the shadows on the east side of the garage. If you WAiNK It, you’ll see it sells for a whopping $23,375 and has an advanced tracker.
Use the Key Cloner to get into the car. Unlocking cars with digital keys is similar to using the Slim Jim to unlock cars with physical keys. Use the right thumbstick to move around the circle until you find the weak spot, indicated by how fast the key clones and the audio cue. Hold it there and the door unlocks, allowing you to enter and drive immediately – no hotwiring required. As Randy said on the call, the only good way to deal with an advanced tracker is to drive fast. You’ll have a very brief grace period after starting the car before the advanced tracker activates. The tracker icon above the minimap begins pulsing and the circle around it fills with red as the tracker activates. Once the ring is completely filled red, the local police are notified about the car’s theft, earning you an instant two-star Wanted level. The only way to prevent activating the tracker is by moving fast, constantly. If you speed up enough as the tracker ring fills, you can cancel the alarm.
Do your best to get out of the area as fast and as safely as possible. Any damage you do to the car now reduces the payout you’ll get for delivering it in perfect condition. One of the best ways to get to Randy with the space to drive fast is by taking the highway. Drive just fast enough so the tracker isn’t getting set off, but not so fast that you can’t control the car. If you set off the advanced tracker of any car, the police respond to the location where it was set off, not where you are exactly as you drive – unless a cop spotted you as the tracker went off. Then they'll pursue you and you'll need to shake them like you would normally. As setting off a tracker only warrants a two-star Wanted level, passing into another district, county, or region puts you and the car in the clear so long as you're not being actively chased by cops. Be sure to keep moving fast, though, because the tracker can go off again if you drive too slow. Advanced tracker signals are blocked near Randy’s showroom, so I’d recommend slowing the cars as you get off the highway to avoid crashing at the last second. Pull into Randy’s garage to deliver the car and get your payment. After taking a look at the car, Randy asks you to join him over at a big whiteboard with “WANTED” written on top. He introduces a list of 15 cars a client of his wants. If you can find and bring the listed cars to Randy in top condition, you can make a lot of money.
Now when you scan cars out in Leonida, you'll get an extra notification if you find a car on Randy’s list. You can see the car list any time in the Robberies menu of the Map, under Randy’s Wish List. We also have a guide with hints on where to find each of the cars. You can talk to Randy more if you’d like, but leave when you’re ready. If you need a car, you can use one of the three branded cars for free just outside the showroom. As you leave, Randy texts you if you earned a condition bonus payment for the car you delivered. If you delivered the Granforma in perfect condition, you’ll get an extra $10,000. With this mission complete, you can now work on a new optional mission called Randy's Wish List. Check IGN's official guide page for help with these vehicles. Now that you have the Key Cloner, practically no civilian car is off limits. If you’re ready to continue with missions, you may have one of these ready to go next: This walkthrough features some first-person elements. Those come from IGN's GTA 6 Lead Editor, Miranda Sanchez. You can learn more about Miranda and her experience on the About the GTA 6 Guide Editors page.

title: GS Caltex Posts 1 Trillion Won in Profit Amid Refining Boom, but Hydrogen Business Results Remain Unclear—What Happened to Vice Chairman Saehong Hur's 2024 Completion Target? - 뉴스필드
content:
English translation of the original Korean report. Images and source documents may contain Korean text. Operating Record of 10,000-Ton Annual-Capacity Liquefied Hydrogen Facility Announced in 2021 Remains Unclear…Yeosu Hydrogen Hub Also Targets Site Completion in 2027 Five years have passed since the hydrogen business championed by GS Caltex Vice Chairman and CEO Saehong Hur as a future growth engine began gaining momentum, yet the commercial operating record of the liquefied hydrogen production facility originally targeted for completion in 2024 remains unclear. According to official announcements by GS Caltex and Korea Gas Corporation (KOGAS) cited on the 23rd, the two companies signed a memorandum of understanding on May 28, 2021, and announced plans to build a liquefied hydrogen production facility with an annual capacity of 10,000 tons at a KOGAS LNG receiving terminal by 2024. At the time, Hur, now vice chairman, outlined a vision of combining the capabilities of the two companies to lead the hydrogen market, while plans were also made to develop fueling infrastructure to supply liquefied hydrogen to the Seoul metropolitan area and central regions of the country. However, as of November this year, five years after the initial announcement, publicly available materials do not establish whether the facility has been completed or how much hydrogen it has actually produced, raising questions about the project’s progress. Meanwhile, GS Caltex reported consolidated third-quarter revenue of KRW 17.7641 trillion and operating profit of KRW 1.1447 trillion in results announced on the 5th, with operating profit increasing 208% from the same period a year earlier. Strong refining margins and improved profitability in the lubricants business supported the earnings performance, but it remains unconfirmed whether the strong performance of the company’s existing businesses has translated into progress toward commercialization of its hydrogen business. ■ Yeosu Hydrogen Hub Also Targets Site Completion in 2027…Separate from Carbon Capture Commercialization In June 2024, GS Caltex signed a land purchase agreement with the Yeosu Gwangyang Port Authority for an approximately 250,000-square-meter site at the Yulchon Convergence Logistics Complex and began pursuing the construction of hydrogen production, power generation and carbon capture facilities. According to a plan released by the Gwangyang Bay Area Free Economic Zone Authority in January of last year, the logistics complex is being developed with a target completion date of 2027, after which construction of hydrogen production, power generation and carbon capture-related facilities is expected to take approximately three years. Separately, GS Caltex is pursuing a project with DIG Airgas to recover carbon dioxide generated during the hydrogen manufacturing process and utilize it as liquid carbon dioxide, forecasting that commercialization in July 2027 will reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 127,000 tons annually. Because this project falls under carbon capture and utilization (CCU) and is distinct from the commercial production of blue hydrogen itself, the progress of the original liquefied hydrogen facility and the actual production commencement schedule of the Yeosu hydrogen hub are expected to serve as key benchmarks for assessing the results of the hydrogen business outlined by Vice Chairman Hur. Meanwhile, Vice Chairman Saehong Hur is the eldest son of Hur Dong-soo, Honorary Chairman and former chairman of GS Caltex, and a fourth-generation executive of GS Group’s founding family. He became CEO of GS Caltex in 2019 and was promoted to vice chairman in GS Group’s regular executive reshuffle for 2026, announced on November 26, 2025. GS Caltex is a joint venture owned equally by GS Energy, a wholly owned subsidiary of the holding company GS Corp., and Chevron-affiliated interests of the U.S. energy company Chevron, each holding a 50% stake. A gap in publicly available information remains between the original completion target for the liquefied hydrogen production facility announced during Hur’s tenure as CEO and the facility’s actual commercialization status. title: 8,502 voter applications filed at two-day SSR camps; Kolathur tops list - DT Next
content: CHENNAI: More than 8,502 physical forms were submitted across 16 Assembly constituencies in Chennai district during the two-day Special Summary Revision (SSR) camps held over the weekend, on November 21 and 22. After releasing the draft electoral roll on November 12, the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) organised special drives at all polling stations on November 21 and 22 to facilitate voter additions, deletions, corrections, and address changes. While 1,698 applications were received on Saturday, the turnout surged on Sunday, with the officials receiving 6,804 forms. During the drive, 5,156 new voter enrolment forms (Form 6) were submitted in bulk, followed by 3,213 requests for address shifting and corrections (Form 8), 132 applications for deletion (Form 7), and one overseas elector form (Form 6A). Among the constituencies, Kolathur recorded the highest turnout with 997 forms, followed by Perambur 751, Virugambakkam 743, Villivakkam 681, and Dr Radhakrishnan Nagar 667. The lowest was recorded in Thiru Vi Ka Nagar with 335. District Election Officer and GCC Commissioner GS Sameeran inspected the special camp at Thiru Vi Ka Higher Secondary School in Shenoy Nagar under the Anna Nagar constituency on Sunday. title: Is it cos we ain't laughing? Ali G's comeback leaves a lifelong fan disappointed - Yahoo News UK
content: With that in mind, and as a huge fan of Ali G, I must admit, after watching the trailers for his new film, Who Iz I? I had very low expectations. Comedy, unlike music, rarely stands the test of time. The Beatles, Nirvana or the Stones can sound as fresh today as the day they were recorded, but comedy? Hits from yesteryear, including Bernard Manning, Are You Being Served?, It Ain't Half Hot Mum and In Sickness and in Health, can look incredibly dated, and offensive, in today's climes, and, sad to say, Ali G now joins that list. There were a few laugh-out-loud moments in the first couple of minutes as flashes of Baron Cohen's genius came flooding back, but afterwards it was a steady demise of the legend, a storyline thought out by a three-year-old in a hurry, and jokes that failed to land time and time again. Brett Ellis gave up watching the new Ali G film (Image: Brett Ellis) Looking jaded and lacking the verve of the original incarnation which showed he had true comedy gahoonas: see the rodeo skit, or the dismantling of celebrities and politicians who, at the time, did not get the joke. Cliché after cliché followed and, I gave up with about 20 minutes to go. It was painful to watch the demise of a fallen idol. I went and did something more interesting by running a virus check on my laptop. Everyone knows who he is, so the element of surprise has gone, hence the poorly scripted nature of this film. He looked under duress and devoid of ideas, like when you see an 80-year-old shuffling down the High Street in a Fubu tracksuit and Air Jordans, and find people are no longer laughing with you, but at you, behind your back. It flopped at the box office, unsurprisingly, and the woke called for its cancellation as they claimed cultural appropriation, which was rarely challenged back in the day as they didn't get the irony that this was a Jewish man poking fun at redneck stereotypes and his own faith. For a legacy to live, you need to leave it alone as coming back when the horse has bolted the stable does little but damage your brand irreversibly, and this is a case in point. Rest in peace Ali G, it was fun whilst it lasted, and you did more for Staines Westside than the Surrey tourist board could have mustered in a millennium, and for that you get my respect. Aiiii. title: Forget The BMW GS — This ADV Gives You Most Of What Matters - Top Speed
content: The big BMW GS is the undisputed leader of the full-size adventure class, dominating sales with decades of updates, massive road presence, and class-setting electronics. Buyers flock to the German flagship because it eats up cross-country miles while projecting serious status at every stop. However, that prestige carries steep initial pricing and expensive dealer service bills, putting it out of reach for riders who prioritize high-mileage dependability over badge appeal. The real question is whether you actually need to spend that kind of money for serious adventure riding. The Suzuki V-Strom 1050DE proves that you can forget the BMW GS and still get most of what actually matters for long-distance travel at a lower price. Its proven 1,037 cc V-twin engine and steel frame skip the dizzying electronic complexity of expensive European rivals, but that straightforward foundation delivers the exact substance you need out in the boondocks: great torque, predictable handling, and bulletproof mechanical longevity. By offering real cross-country competence, distinct character, and rock-solid reliability for a fraction of the cost, Suzuki skips the marketing hype entirely and gives riders everything that actually counts from the GS’s arsenal. That value-first philosophy becomes even clearer when you put its sticker price next to Munich’s flagship. The big V-Strom range starts at $15,699, but that is for the base model with alloy wheels. The 'DE' signifies its off-road intentions, and you get a spoke rim combination with tires more compatible with the dirt. This model has a base price of $16,649. There's no question that the R 1300 GS is the adventure bike benchmark, but it also asks for a lot more money for its modern features like Bluetooth, navigation, and electronic suspension, and shaft drive. The base model costs $20,395, and when you start adding options and accessories to it, you are sucked into the world of BMW's packages. It will very easily drive the price up to $25,000. In effect, the Suzuki offers most of what the BMW has to offer, but at nearly half the price. Suzuki has stuck with a V-twin engine for the V-Strom 1050DE, and this is one of the coolest examples of that engine layout. This is a 90-degree V-twin that displaces 1,037 cc, has liquid cooling, and a DOHC setup. It is a short-stroke design with a compression ratio of 11.5:1 to produce 107.4 horsepower at 8,500 RPM and 73.7 pound-feet of torque at 6,000 RPM. This V-twin does not have best-in-class power figures, but it generates most of its performance low in the rev range. For an adventure motorcycle, that is incredibly good news. The result will be lower stress and therefore better longevity and better fuel economy. It is mated to a six-speed gearbox with an assist and slipper clutch that also has hydraulic actuation. The V-Strom 1050DE chooses an old-school chassis that matches its Honda-like reliability with BMW touring comfort. This is an aluminum twin-spar frame, which is expensive to produce and heavier than the frames other adventure bikes use today, but the flip side is that the V-Strom 1050 offers some of the best feel and feedback among the competition. The suspension is provided by KYB: 43 mm inverted forks with 6.7 inches of travel and a link-type rear shock with 6.6 inches of travel. Both ends are fully adjustable. The brakes consist of twin 310 mm front discs with radial four-piston fixed Tokico calipers and a 260 mm rear disc with a Nissin single-piston caliper. These are linked brakes, which is a great feature at the price. It uses spoked rims with a 21-inch front and 17-inch rear, where you'll find one of the V-Strom's quirks: only the rear rim is tubeless. The V-Strom 1050DE is 94 inches long with a height of 59.3 inches. The seat height is 34.6 inches, and the ground clearance is 7.5 inches. It has a wheelbase of 62.8 inches, weighs 554 pounds wet, and the fuel tank can hold 5.3 gallons of fuel. These are the dimensions of a normal full-size adventure motorcycle. The seat height and ground clearance are normal for the segment, while the wheelbase is a little long for the segment, which should make it very stable at speed. That is added to by its weight. All said and done, this is a very comfortable two-up tourer that feels built for riders over 60, but don’t expect it to change direction with as much ease as the competition. The V-Strom 1050DE offers just enough features to make it an enjoyable premium experience, but it does not go overboard since V-Strom owners don't care about fancy gadgets. It leads with the five-inch TFT display, but it leaves out Bluetooth and navigation. The engine has a by-wire throttle with three ride modes, cruise control, and switchable cornering traction control. Of course, the brakes might be linked, but the rear ABS can be switched off as well. The standard equipment includes a center stand, the aluminum skid plate, the engine crash bar, and a tool-adjustable windscreen. The options list includes a taller touring windscreen, the quick-release screen adjustment kit, upper crash bars, and hard or soft luggage. We want to hear from you. title: A-G’s directive on suspects’ rights must translate into action, not just promises – Sulemana Braimah - MyJoyOnline
content: The Executive Director of the Media Foundation for West Africa (MFWA), Sulemana Braimah, has cautioned that the Attorney-General’s directive on protecting the rights of arrested persons must be backed by effective enforcement to produce meaningful results. He said although the directive reinforces important constitutional and legal safeguards, its success would depend on whether law enforcement agencies translate the requirements into their daily operations. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 21, Mr Braimah welcomed the directive, describing decisions aimed at promoting and protecting people's rights as fundamental. However, he questioned why law enforcement agencies had, over the years, failed to consistently uphold requirements that were already captured in existing laws. The Attorney-General's directive requires law enforcement and investigative agencies, including the Ghana Police Service, the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO), the National Intelligence Bureau (NIB) and the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC), to comply with the constitutional 48-hour detention limit and other safeguards protecting suspects. It also requires arrested persons to be informed of the reasons for their arrest and their right to legal representation, while prohibiting the use of arrest and detention to recover civil debts, unlawful searches, torture and coercion. The agencies are further required to respect suspects' right to silence and ensure that confessions are voluntary, while submitting quarterly compliance reports to the Attorney-General detailing arrests, releases, court appearances and alleged rights violations. Mr Braimah said the directive was a welcome development but warned against allowing it to become another official declaration that generates public expectations without producing tangible changes. “The challenge is whether or not it is going to be one of those usual things where nice policy statements are made, nice declarations and directives are issued and at the end of the day we are just back to square one,” he said. He argued that the real achievement would be seen when citizens begin to experience improved protection of their rights in their dealings with law enforcement agencies. Drawing a comparison with political party manifestoes, he said governments often presented attractive promises and policies but failed to deliver the expected changes after assuming office. Mr Braimah therefore maintained that the Attorney-General's directive should be judged by its practical outcomes rather than the announcement itself. He also acknowledged that enforcing the requirements could prove more difficult in practice than it appeared on paper, making sustained commitment from the affected institutions essential. He stressed that while the directive deserved recognition, meaningful acknowledgement would only be justified when its implementation began to produce visible results for the protection of citizens' rights.

title: UNI GS Christy Hoffman to speak at Paris Summit Against International Oligarchy - UNI Global Union
content:
20.11.26 UNI General Secretary Christy Hoffman will speak at the first Paris Summit Against International Oligarchy on Saturday 21 November 2026 at the Théâtre de la Concorde. The summit was initiated by the International Tax Observatory, led by economist Gabriel Zucman. It brings together economists, researchers, politicians, journalists, trade unionists and activists to debate how to respond to extreme wealth and the concentration of economic, media and technological power. Hoffman will take part in the opening debate, “IA : pour une propriété universelle des savoirs” (AI: for universal ownership of knowledge), at 11.30 a.m. She will be joined by sociologist Isabelle Ferreras of the University of Louvain and economist Cecilia Rikap of University College London, along with a keynote address by Nobel Prize-winning economist Esther Duflo. The panel will ask who owns the knowledge that AI draws on, how the value it generates should be shared and how to stop the technology from concentrating power even further. Hoffman will argue that much of that knowledge comes from workers, whose calls and keystrokes are being recorded to train AI systems, and that they need a say in how it is used and their fair share of what it earns. “When I started work, I could not have imagined how much more power billionaires would accumulate over the following decades, and AI is now accelerating that concentration. We cannot afford a failure of imagination now, because this power is becoming more entrenched by the day. The answer must be as global as the problem, and a critical part of it is stronger unions. Workers must have real power over how companies are run, and the public must have real control over the systems we all depend on. There should be no ceiling on how just and democratic our economies can become. I’m coming to Paris to help widen what our movement believes is possible.” Other speakers at the anti-oligarchy summit include Nobel laureates Paul Krugman, Joseph Stiglitz and Duflo as well as labour leaders such as SEIU-UHW President Dave Regan and the CGT General Secretary Sophie Binet. The day’s debates draw on a manifesto signed by around 100 intellectuals and published on the eve of the summit. title: Judge orders ICE not to move Xie, a Princeton Ph.D. student and asylum seeker, out of Virginia - The Daily Princetonian
content: A federal judge ordered U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement late Friday to not remove Eva Yi Xie GS from the Eastern District of Virginia barring a further court order. The judge, Anthony Trenga ’71, also ordered ICE to respond to a petition for habeas corpus filed by Xie’s lawyers by 5 p.m. on Wednesday. Xie is a third-year Princeton neuroscience Ph.D. student who was detained by ICE at an airport in Virginia on Thursday after departing the Society for Neuroscience’s annual conference in Washington, D.C. She is being held at an ICE holding facility in Chantilly, Va. Xie, who was born in China, came to the United States in 2016 on a visa, when she was a minor. Though her original nonimmigrant status has expired, she has a pending asylum claim and an immigration court date set for early 2028, according to her lawyer, Kerry Doyle. Trenga did not immediately respond to a request for comment. ICE did not respond to multiple requests for comment on Thursday and Friday. During the current Trump administration, ICE has frequently moved detainees away from the districts in which they were detained, but Trenga’s order prohibits that from happening to Xie. Mahmoud Khalil, who was detained in New York in March 2025 as a recent Columbia University graduate, was transferred to a detention facility in Jena, La. as his case was being heard. Khalil was a prominent organizer of the pro-Palestine encampments at Columbia. Rümeysa Öztürk, a Tufts University student detained by ICE in March 2025, was also brought to Louisiana from Massachusetts. Öztürk’s student visa was revoked by the U.S. government largely due to an op-ed she co-authored in The Tufts Daily, the university’s student newspaper, that was critical of the university’s response to the Gaza war. Xie does not appear to have been outspoken on political issues at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, where she was an undergraduate student, nor at Princeton. THIS IS A BREAKING NEWS UPDATE. The Daily Princetonian’s original story follows below. Eva Yi Xie GS, a third-year Princeton neuroscience Ph.D. student who was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Virginia on Thursday, is an asylum seeker who has an immigration court date set for early 2028, her lawyer Kerry Doyle told The Daily Princetonian on Friday afternoon. A habeas corpus petition has been filed in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia by Xie’s lawyers. Xie was detained at the Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Arlington, Va., after departing from the Society for Neuroscience annual conference, where she presented a poster on Wednesday. Rupert Li, a mathematics Ph.D. student at Stanford University who Xie is in a relationship with, told the ‘Prince’ that Xie was planning to board a domestic flight to the San Francisco International Airport to visit him. Doyle, who was arranged to represent Xie by the University, said ICE has not informed her of a reason for the arrest. ICE did not respond to multiple requests for comment on Thursday and Friday. The law office of Parastoo Golesorkhi Zahedi, based in Virginia, is also representing Xie. Doyle previously served as a principal legal adviser for ICE and as deputy general counsel of the Department of Homeland Security during the Biden administration. She is a partner at the law firm Green & Spiegel. Xie is currently being held at an ICE holding center in Chantilly, Va. She has been there since she was detained Thursday afternoon, according to Doyle. Holding centers are not fully equipped detention facilities, and they are meant to be a temporary holding location. Xie arrived in the United States from China in 2016, when she was a minor, and attended the Bronx High School of Science. She later attended the Massachusetts Institute of Technology as an undergraduate. Doyle said that Xie’s family applied for asylum within a year of arriving. The asylum claim was referred to immigration court, though Doyle said she does not yet know when that referral occurred. In the habeas corpus filing, according to Doyle, Xie’s lawyers argued that ICE detained her without a warrant. They claimed that because Xie did not have a recent change in circumstances or pose an imminent risk of leaving the country that would make a warrantless arrest necessary, Xie should be released. According to Doyle, holding facilities like the one in Chantilly don’t have accommodations like readily accessible beds and showers, making them incompatible for long-term detention. She called it “completely inhumane” to hold people at processing facilities for extended periods. In August 2026, immigration advocacy organizations reported poor conditions at the Virginia facility. The American Civil Liberties Union reported that up to 80 people were held in a single room for longer than a week without access to lawyers, medical care, or basic hygiene. Since Xie’s detention, members of the University community have advocated for her release. Princeton graduate students and Xie’s lab have called for people to send messages to politicians in New Jersey and Virginia about the case. New Jersey Senator Andy Kim’s office is directly in touch with Xie, according to Kim’s press secretary Katey Sabo. She added that his office is “working on the case” in a statement to the ‘Prince.’ Sen. Cory Booker, the other New Jersey senator, wrote in a statement to the ‘Prince’ that ICE has not responded to his outreach on Xie’s detention. Kim and Booker are both Democrats. “My office has contacted U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) regarding the detention of Eva Yi Xie and has not yet received a response. I expect a prompt and full explanation of the circumstances surrounding her detention,” Booker wrote. Wynne Stagnaro GS, a member of Xie’s lab, shared in an interview with the ‘Prince’ that Xie’s advisor, Carlos Brody, has said she is remaining calm about the situation. “‘She’s amazing, steady as a rock,’” Stagnaro said Brody wrote after speaking with Xie. “I really want Eva to be able to be back and to be able to live her life and to be able to celebrate the holiday. It’s really jarring and something that I don’t think should be happening,” Stagnaro added. İnci Çetin GS, who serves on the policy subcommittee of the Faculty Committee on the Graduate School alongside Xie, had been on a call with other graduate students right before she spoke with the ‘Prince.’ She shared in an interview that Xie has been a strong leader for the graduate student body. “She’s a really engaged person. She always brought up important issues … to the community, and she was vocal about it,” Çetin said. The Society for Neuroscience, which organized the conference Xie was attending, wrote in a statement that it was “closing monitoring the detention.” “We are in close contact with Princeton University and stand ready to provide any support that may be needed. Our thoughts are with Eva, her family, and her colleagues,” the Society added. “News of Eva’s detention is distressing for me and many members of the Princeton University community,” Dean of the Graduate School Rodney Priestley wrote in a statement to the ‘Prince.’ “We will remain in contact with her legal team, her family, and colleagues to provide support.” “We hope Eva will soon be able to resume her studies at Princeton,” Priestley added. title: Lewis Hamilton Says He Flew an F-16 at 9.5 Gs and Texted Tom Cruise About Top Gun 3 - Yahoo
content: Lewis Hamilton has been swapping the cockpit of a Ferrari for that of a fighter jet. The seven-time world champion told a Las Vegas crowd he had just flown an F-16, and that the flight pulled 9.5 Gs, or nine and a half times the normal pull of gravity on his body. It is the kind of force that tests even a trained athlete. He shared the story at a fan forum ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix while answering questions about life after racing, footage of which was shared by praveenrandev on Instagram. Hamilton started by saying that he was working on the second F1 movie. On the jet, he said: "I just went up in a fighter jet, and I texted Tom [Cruise], I'm ready for Top Gun 3. I was like, 'I've got to be involved.'" "I definitely could do it. I flew the F16. 9.5 Gs, baby," he added. Nov 21, 2025; Las Vegas, NV, USA; Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton (44) is introduced before the Las Vegas Grand Prix at Las Vegas Strip Circuit. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. He has also said of the third film: "I will miss a race for it." Paramount has since announced that Top Gun 3 is in development with Cruise and producer Jerry Bruckheimer, so his timing looks better now. title: Peterborough theatre history brought to life in free exhibition - Peterborough Matters
content:
David G-S as Fairy Godmother (Image: Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery) David G-S as Fairy Godmother (Image: Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery) A new exhibition is shining a spotlight on centuries of theatre history in Peterborough. Life’s a Stage, opening at Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery on 21 November 2026, explores the city’s theatrical heritage from the late 1700s to the present day. The exhibition runs until February 20, 2027, and features playbills, archive materials, and memorabilia from venues including the long-lost Theatre Royal, Hippodrome, and Embassy Theatre, as well as modern stages like The Crescent, The New Theatre, and the Key Theatre. Glenys Wass, heritage collections museum manager, said: "We are delighted to share this fascinating exhibition with our visitors. Cast of Cinderella (Image: Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery) "We have enjoyed working with current staff at Landmark Theatres and The Cresset to develop the exhibition, along with hearing memories shared by past employees to create this exhibition. "We hope people have as much fun visiting it as we did creating it." Visitors can learn about the families who managed the theatres, the performers who graced the stages, and the evolution of Peterborough’s theatrical scene. The exhibition also celebrates the city’s pantomime tradition, with props and costumes from past productions and a mini stage where guests can take part in the fun. Life's A Stage (Image: Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery) Famous names who once performed in Peterborough, including Vera Lynn, George Formby, and Laurel and Hardy—who visited in 1952—are featured in the displays. To mark the opening, the museum will be welcoming a very special guest appearance from 'The Fairy Godmother,' Dame from this year’s Cinderella pantomime at Landmark Theatre’s New Theatre, who will be joining the launch alongside one of her naughty elves. Visitors will have the chance to meet the characters and pose for photos on Saturday, November 21, between 10am and 12 noon. The exhibition is free to attend at Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery. title: Karol G's medical condition that causes weight gain: "People shouldn't care, I'm a singer" - MARCA
content: Karol G's medical condition that causes weight gain: "People shouldn't care, I'm a singer" The artist revealed it this way in her Netflix documentary titled "Tomorrow Was Very Beautiful" Singer Karol G is in one of the best moments of her professional career. Her songs and shows are a success, and projects keep multiplying in her career. One of them, without a doubt, is the appearance of her song "El Makinón" in the GTA VI video game. However, the artist has had moments in which she has not felt very well and has had health problems. Recently, she has had to postpone her concert in Mexico City due to a health issue that, according to some media outlets' speculation, could be the flu. However, in her documentary titled "Tomorrow Was Very Beautiful", she mentioned that she has another underlying health problem that "causes weight gain," an issue for which she has often been criticized, in her own words. The illness the artist suffers from, according to what she herself said, is insulin resistance, in addition to the hormonal imbalances she experiences. These two conditions work and interact in many ways but, one of them, is body weight. Insulin resistance promotes fat storage since, when cells respond poorly to insulin, the pancreas produces more to compensate. This excess, as Dr. Jorge Solano mentions, drives the body to store energy as fat and slows the use of this fuel. In addition, it is normal for those who suffer from this problem to feel an increase in hunger and cravings, due to fluctuations in glucose and insulin. On the other hand, it is normal for fat to accumulate in the abdominal and visceral area. All of this complicates weight loss and weight maintenance which, added to the hormonal imbalance, can present a fairly complex situation to deal with, especially when you have a great deal of public exposure. People shouldn't care how much weight, because I'm a singer, I'm not a model Aesthetic pressure is one of the issues women have to deal with in almost every area of their lives. One of those areas is the music industry. In that regard, many artists feel that there is a double standard when it comes to what is demanded of a man and a woman who have the same profession. Almost no man feels the scrutiny that women are subjected to in the artistic sphere. Additionally, in many cases, they feel they suffer from ageism and that natural aging penalizes women, as many women have mentioned in interviews. On the other hand, the pressure not only comes from outside, but in many cases, it is also exerted from "home". The important thing is to understand that we should not comment on other people's bodies without knowing the context, reason, or cause of a physical change. The reality is that it can have a mental health impact on the artist, which can cause anxiety and emotional strain. © 2026  Unidad Editorial Información Deportiva, S.L.U. All rights reserved. title: Chennai: Functional RWH systems now must for completion certificate - The New Indian Express
content: CHENNAI: Completion certificates for buildings in the city will be issued only after officials verify that their rainwater harvesting structures are functional, and not merely present, Greater Chennai Corporation Commissioner G S Sameeran said on Thursday. He was speaking on the sidelines of a stakeholder meeting by civic body with the Confederation of Real Estate Developers’ Associations of India (CREDAI), the Chennai Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (CMWSSB), resident welfare associations and NGOs, to promote rainwater harvesting as part of the ‘Thuli’ people’s movement. According to a CMWSSB survey of 10 lakh properties, only six lakh had functional rainwater harvesting structures. The corporation aims to raise the number to 13-14 lakh buildings, covering at least 70% of the 17 lakh assessed properties in the city, wherever feasible, particularly in larger buildings. Sameeran said a government order (G.O. 193) issued by the municipal administration and water supply department on January 2 lays down schematic diagrams and guidelines on construction of rainwater harvesting structures based on soil types. Copies of the order will be distributed to RWAs, and residents will be trained in maintaining and repairing the structures, he said. Chennai requires 1,246 million litres per day (MLD) of water, of which around 80% comes from reservoirs such as Poondi, Puzhal and Chembarambakkam, around 12% from desalination plants and around 6% from groundwater, he said. The groundwater level was recorded at 5.6 m above the aquifer in 2026 against 7.9 m during previous years of heavy rainfall, he said. Despite receiving 612 mm of rainfall against the city’s annual requirement of 850 mm, reservoir storage remains low at an average of 41% against the usual level of around 60%, and the corporation is pinning hopes on the rain between November 23 and 26 to replenish them. Asked about the poor maintenance of rainwater harvesting structures, Sameeran said the GCC had created such facilities in 1,858 buildings, 1,013 parks, 87 major playgrounds and along 30,000 stormwater drains covering 3,000 km, but some had been damaged over time. On the structures developed using German technology at the wells of the Vadapalani and Chitrakulam temples, which were later left unattended, he said there were two types of sponge parks, and the one using eco-blocks with a honeycomb-like structure may not be suitable everywhere since they are made of plastic. The corporation is also rejuvenating 245 ponds and plans to develop sponge parks using the natural gradients of the land at locations such as playgrounds. title: Princeton neuroscience Ph.D. student detained by ICE - The Daily Princetonian
content: Eva Yi Xie GS, a third-year Ph.D. student in neuroscience, has been detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement at an airport near Washington, D.C. She is believed to be held in a detention center in Chantilly, Va. Xie is the first known Princeton student to be reported to be detained by ICE. “The University has arranged for legal counsel to represent the student,” University spokesperson Michael Hotchkiss wrote in a statement to The Daily Princetonian Thursday night. The Society for Neuroscience annual conference was held in Washington, D.C., from Saturday through Wednesday. Xie presented a poster at the conference on Wednesday titled “Entorhinal grid-like coding generalizes to jointly organize physical and cognitive dimensions.” Xie is a member of the Brody Lab. She is advised by neuroscience professor Carlos Brody and coadvised by neuroscience professor Nathaniel Daw and computer science professor Benjamin Eysenbach. “It seems wildly unfair,” Brody wrote in a statement to the ‘Prince.’ “Eva is a brilliant law-abiding student and wonderful person who has many talents to contribute to the United States. Detaining her, with the intent of deporting her, makes no sense whatsoever. It is cruel, and it is our country shooting itself in the foot.” Dean of the Graduate School Rodney Priestley emailed graduate students in the Princeton Neuroscience Institute about the incident at 11:01 p.m. Thursday evening. “We hope she is able to soon resume her studies at Princeton,” the email, obtained by The Daily Princetonian, read. “Please be assured that we will stay in close contact with the student’s family, her legal team, and her PNI colleagues as this situation is resolved.” Wynne Stagnaro GS, a fellow PNI graduate student in the Brody Lab, shared specifics of the incident in a message on the Graduate Student Government Slack. According to Stagnaro, Xie sent a “call for help” to her lab mates via Slack Thursday afternoon. She told the ‘Prince’ on Friday morning that the lab mates have been able to make contact with Xie. “Eva is a brilliant computational and experimental systems neuroscientist. She is also a valued colleague, mentor, and friend, and we are privileged that she chose our lab for her thesis research,” Stagnaro wrote in her message. “She went to a conference to present her work, and now she’s in a detention center. She should be home.” An X post from the Brody Lab shared similar sentiments. Stagnaro shared that members of the Brody Lab have been in touch with the office of Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., other elected officials, and members of the media. Stagnaro did not add anything beyond the Slack post in a statement to the ‘Prince.’ Xie is researching the “neural basis of decision-making.” She emigrated from China to the U.S. in 2016. She graduated from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 2024 with double majors in computer science and mathematics and a concentration in economics. She has interned with Meta, Microsoft AI, and IBM Research, among others. At MIT, Xie was one of three undergraduates elected to the Presidential Advisory Cabinet for Institute President Sally Kornbluth and chaired the MIT Judicial Review Board. She is now on the Policy Subcommittee of the Princeton Graduate Student Committee on the Graduate School. Xie previously organized a workshop called “Data on the Brain & Mind” for the 2025 Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems. She is currently co-organizing the Annual Conference on Cognitive Computational Neuroscience for 2027 in Edinburgh, Scotland. Eysenbach and Daw could not immediately be reached for comment. ICE did not respond to multiple requests for comment.
